questions.stem: An objective has the term 200 x_a x_b, with x_a and x_b binary. The term is replaced by 200 z with z binary. Which rows make z equal x_a x_b at every 0/1 point?

options.text: z >= x_a, z >= x_b and z <= x_a + x_b
options.says: These rows make z the OR of the two: z = 1 when only one is 1, where the product is 0.

options.text: z = x_a + x_b - 1, with no other row
options.says: With both at 0 this asks for z = -1, which a binary cannot take, so the plan with neither is refused.

options.text: z <= x_a + x_b and z >= x_a - x_b
options.says: With x_a = 1 and x_b = 0 these rows force z = 1, where the product is 0.

options.text: z <= x_a, z <= x_b and z >= x_a + x_b - 1
options.says: Right: these are the AND rows, and the product of two binaries is their AND.

origin.section: A Product of Two Binaries Is Their AND, Written as Three Rows

questions.stem: A maximization subtracts $300k for each pair of projects whose outages fall in the same week, as -300 z_ab, and the only rows on z_ab are z_ab <= x_a and z_ab <= x_b. What does the solver do with z_ab?

options.text: It keeps z_ab equal to x_a x_b, since the rows tie it to both projects
options.says: Those rows only push z_ab down; nothing pushes it up when both projects are funded.

options.text: It sets z_ab to 1 with one project funded, charging a cost never incurred
options.says: z_ab <= x_a and z_ab <= x_b forbid z_ab = 1 unless both are funded, and the cost makes 1 unattractive anyway.

options.text: It leaves z_ab at 0 with both funded, so the cost is never charged
options.says: Right: the cost pushes z_ab down and only z_ab >= x_a + x_b - 1 would stop it, as with the transmission pairs.

options.text: It finds no plan, since no z_ab can satisfy both rows at once
options.says: z_ab = 0 satisfies both rows for every plan, so the model is never infeasible because of them.

origin.section: The Sign of the Product's Term Decides Which Rows It Needs

questions.stem: A model has w = x q with x binary and q between 2 and 10. An analyst writes the four product rows with 100 in place of 10. What changes?

options.text: The 0/1 plans change, since w can now exceed q when x = 1
options.says: With x = 1 the rows w <= q and w >= q still hold, so w = q; only the LP relaxation sees the 100.

options.text: The 0/1 plans stay the same, and the LP bound can get looser
options.says: Right: any bound at least the true one is exact at 0/1 points, and a larger one admits more fractional points.

options.text: Nothing changes, since the solver finds the tightest bound by itself
options.says: The LP relaxation uses the number written in the rows; with 60 in place of 6 the GridCap LP bound rose.

options.text: The model finds no plan, since 100 is outside the range of q
options.says: The bound in a row only needs to be at least the largest q; a number above it never cuts off a plan.

origin.section: The Bounds in the Rows Are Part of the Formulation
